title: Chiropractic Clinic Scope Tasks: High-Touch and Floor Maintenance Routines for Chiropractic & Wellness Clinics
seoTitle: Chiropractic Clinic Scope Tasks: Daily, Weekly & Monthly Checklist
metaDescription: Chiropractic clinic scope tasks by frequency, with minutes per task and the specialty work that adds $35-$95/hr labor. Price your scope in our calculator.
excerpt: A chiropractic clinic scope of work has to cover adjusting tables, face cradles, rehab equipment, and busy restrooms that a generic office checklist ignores. This guide breaks the work into nightly, weekly, and monthly tasks and shows which ones add billable labor hours.
quickAnswer: A chiropractic clinic scope should list nightly disinfection of every adjusting table, face cradle, and armrest, full restroom sanitation, trash removal, and vacuuming plus damp mopping of all treatment rooms. Weekly and monthly tasks such as baseboard detailing, rehab equipment wipe-downs, glass partitions, and machine scrubbing of LVT add labor that vendors bill at $35-$65 per hour for standard work and $55-$95 per hour for specialty tasks.

blocks.text: What makes a chiropractic scope different from an office checklist

A standard office scope assumes desks, a breakroom, and restrooms used by the same 30 people every day. A chiropractic clinic flips that ratio. Staff headcount is small, but patient volume is high, and every patient touches the reception counter, the check-in tablet, a chair, a restroom, and at least one treatment surface. The scope of work must therefore be organized around patient-contact surfaces first and general dusting second. If a proposal lists only generic office tasks, the vendor has not priced your treatment rooms, and quality will slide within weeks.

The other difference is the equipment. Drop tables have moving sections, flexion-distraction tables have hinges and padded rollers, decompression units have harness straps, and many clinics now run hydro-massage beds, cold-laser carts, and rehab zones with mats, balls, and resistance bands. Cleaners do not service clinical devices, but they must wipe exterior housings, upholstery, and the floor around and under them. That is where the extra minutes come from.

These tasks happen every service visit, whether the contract is twice weekly or five nights a week. Times shown assume a two- to three-doctor clinic of about 3,200 sq ft with six adjusting rooms and two restrooms.

blocks.caption: Nightly chiropractic clinic scope tasks with typical labor minutes per visit
rows: Disinfect table tops, face cradles, armrests, and headpiece paper rollers; wipe stools and chair arms
Vacuum or dust-mop, then damp mop LVT under and around tables
Disinfect counter, check-in tablet, pens, door levers; straighten chairs; vacuum entry mats
Clean and disinfect toilets, sinks, grab bars, dispensers; restock; mop floor
Wipe mats, balance boards, and equipment handles; dust-mop rubber floor
Empty trash and recycling, wipe breakroom counters and sink, spot clean microwave
Trash and liner change in all rooms, check sharps container levels and report to staff

blocks.text: Add those ranges and a nightly visit for this clinic takes roughly 107 to 144 minutes of labor, or about 1.8 to 2.4 crew hours. That is well below the ISSA production benchmark of 3,500 sq ft per hour for open office space, because treatment rooms are small, furniture-dense, and full of surfaces that must stay wet for a disinfectant's label contact time.

blocks.title: Sharps are not janitorial
blocks.text: If your clinic offers dry needling or acupuncture, the crew should only check sharps container fill levels and report them. Removal and disposal belong to a licensed medical waste hauler. Write that boundary into the scope so a cleaner never handles a full sharps box.
Weekly tasks that keep surfaces from degrading

items: Detail baseboards and corners in all treatment rooms and corridors with an angled flagged-bristle broom such as the O-Cedar Commercial MaxiClean, whose 12-inch head and 48-inch handle reach under tables without the crew kneeling.
Wipe adjusting table bases, hydraulic columns, foot pedals, and wheels where lint and hair accumulate.
Squeegee interior glass partitions, the reception sneeze guard, and entry doors; a 14-inch solid brass Ettore squeegee with replaceable rubber leaves streak-free glass in one pass.
Scrub breakroom sink and restroom porcelain stains with non-rusting Scotch-Brite heavy-duty pads rather than steel wool, which scratches and leaves rust marks.
Dust high surfaces: anatomy models, X-ray viewing boxes, wall-mounted TVs, vent grilles, and door tops.
Wipe treatment-room upholstery seams and decompression harness exteriors with a vinyl-safe disinfectant.
Clean inside trash receptacles and replace liners in high-volume restrooms.

blocks.text: Weekly tasks typically add 60 to 90 minutes, either as a longer visit one night per week or spread across visits. On a three-times-weekly contract with 13 visits per month, that works out to about 4.3 to 6.5 additional crew hours per month. At standard rates of $35-$65 per hour, the weekly detail list alone is worth $150-$420 per month, so confirm it appears in the proposal rather than as an assumed courtesy.
Monthly and quarterly tasks: where specialty labor lives

blocks.caption: Periodic chiropractic clinic tasks and how vendors typically bill them
rows: Machine scrub and buff LVT or VCT in treatment rooms and corridors
Specialty hourly $55-$95 or included in deep floor program
Hot-water extraction of office and waiting-room carpet
$0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month amortized
Deep clean hydro-massage bed exterior and surrounding tile
High dusting of light fixtures and HVAC diffusers

blocks.text: For a 3,200 sq ft clinic, amortized deep floor care at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month adds $96-$192 per month. That is usually cheaper than calling for one-off extraction after a muddy winter, which is often priced at a separate trip minimum.
Which tasks push labor above standard office rates

Vendors split chiropractic labor into two buckets. Standard work, such as trash, vacuuming, restrooms, and dusting, is priced like any office at $35-$65 per hour. Specialty work, priced at $55-$95 per hour, includes disinfecting patient-contact upholstery to label contact time, cleaning around rehab equipment, machine floor care, and grout restoration. In the nightly table above, about 34 to 45 minutes per visit fall into the specialty bucket. On a 13-visit month that is 7.4 to 9.8 specialty hours, or roughly $407-$931 per month of labor that a generic office bid would never include.

items.name: Inventory treatment surfaces
items.text: Count tables, decompression units, massage beds, and rehab stations, and give the count to every bidder in writing.

items.name: Assign nightly vs. periodic
items.text: Mark each task nightly, weekly, monthly, or quarterly so bids are built on the same frequency assumptions.

items.name: Separate specialty labor
items.text: Ask vendors to show standard and specialty hours separately so you can see whether treatment rooms were truly priced.

items.name: Define staff vs. crew duties
items.text: Document that clinical staff handle between-patient wipes, linens, and device disinfection; the crew handles nightly deep wipes and floors.

items.name: Inspect against the checklist
items.text: Run a monthly walkthrough with the vendor supervisor, scoring each room against the written scope.

blocks.title: Use a room card
blocks.text: Post a laminated card inside each adjusting room closet listing the nightly tasks and the disinfectant contact time. Night crews turn over, and a room card keeps the face cradle and table base from being skipped when a new cleaner starts.

faqs.q: Should the janitorial crew or clinic staff disinfect adjusting tables?
faqs.a: Both, at different times. Clinical staff should wipe the table and face cradle between every patient with an EPA-registered disinfectant. The janitorial crew performs a nightly deep wipe of the entire table, including bases, armrests, and seams, plus the floor underneath. Put both duties in writing so neither side assumes the other is covering it.

faqs.q: How many hours does it take to clean a 3,200 sq ft chiropractic clinic?
faqs.a: A typical nightly visit takes about 1.8 to 2.4 crew hours when the clinic has six treatment rooms and two restrooms. Weekly detail work adds 60 to 90 minutes per week. Converted with 4.333 weeks per month, a three-times-weekly contract runs roughly 28 to 38 labor hours per month before periodic floor care.

faqs.q: What chemicals should be listed in a chiropractic cleaning scope?
faqs.a: The scope should name an EPA-registered disinfectant compatible with vinyl upholstery, a neutral floor cleaner for LVT or wood, and a glass cleaner. Require the vendor to keep Safety Data Sheets on site under OSHA HazCom and to label every secondary spray bottle. Some clinics also request Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice products for general cleaning to reduce odor in small treatment rooms.

faqs.q: Are carpet extraction and floor stripping included in the monthly price?
faqs.a: Usually not unless the contract includes a deep floor program. Many vendors amortize quarterly extraction or scrub-and-recoat at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month. Otherwise these are billed as separate projects. Confirm in writing which approach your vendor uses and how many service events per year are included.

faqs.q: What should a chiropractic scope explicitly exclude?
faqs.a: Typical exclusions are sharps disposal, laundering of linens and gowns, cleaning or disinfecting clinical devices such as ultrasound or laser heads, entry into active X-ray rooms, and exterior windows. Listing exclusions prevents disputes and lets you price those services separately with the right specialist.
